details:
**Mjolnir**
Thor's hammer, which can level mountains and always returns to his hand when thrown. It was forged by the dwarves Brokkr and Eitri (Sindri) in a contest Loki arranged against the Sons of Ivaldi. Loki, in the form of a fly or gadfly, bit Brokkr's eyelid during the forging, so the hammer's handle came out too short, which is why it is wielded with one hand.

**Disguised as Freya to recover his hammer from Thrym**
In the Eddic poem Thrymskvida, the giant Thrym steals Mjolnir and demands the goddess Freya as his bride in exchange. On Heimdall's advice, Thor dresses as the bride, with Loki as his maid; Loki explains away "Freya's" huge appetite and fierce red eyes by claiming she had not eaten or slept for eight nights out of excitement. When the hammer is laid in the bride's lap to bless the wedding, Thor seizes it and kills Thrym and his family.

**Killing Jormungandr at Ragnarok**
Thor's archenemy is the Midgard Serpent Jormungandr, Loki's monstrous son that encircles the world. At Ragnarok Thor kills the serpent but is poisoned by its venom, walks nine steps, and dies.

**Fishing with Hymir**
Thor went fishing with the giant Hymir, ripping the head off Hymir's best ox to use as bait, and hooked the Midgard Serpent. The terrified Hymir cut the line before Thor could kill it. The trip was part of a quest with Tyr to obtain a cauldron large enough for the sea god Aegir to brew ale for the gods, during which Thor smashed a goblet or chalice against Hymir's skull.

**Contests at Utgard-Loki's hall**
On a journey to Jotunheim, Thor slept with his companions inside what turned out to be the glove of the giant Skrymir and failed three times to kill him with his hammer. At Utgard-Loki's hall, Thor failed to empty a drinking horn (its end was in the sea), could lift only one paw of a gray cat (the Midgard Serpent in disguise), and lost a wrestling match to the old woman Elli (old age itself). Skrymir turned out to be Utgard-Loki in disguise.

**Alviss**
A dwarf who wanted to marry Thor's daughter Thrud. In the Alvissmal, Thor quizzed him about the names of things in different worlds until dawn, when the sunlight turned the dwarf to stone.

**Tanngnjostr and Tanngrisnir**
Thor's two goats, "Teeth-barer" and "Teeth-grinder," which pull his chariot. Thor can eat them and resurrect them by blessing their bones and skins with Mjolnir. When Thjalfi, son of the farmer Egil, broke a thigh bone to suck out the marrow, one goat came back lame, so Thjalfi and his sister Roskva became Thor's servants as compensation.

**Sif's golden hair**
Thor's wife Sif had her hair cut off by Loki as a prank. Thor forced Loki to replace it, so Loki had the Sons of Ivaldi make a new head of hair from real gold, which led to the creation of Mjolnir and other treasures.

**Harbard**
A ferryman (Odin in disguise) who refused to take Thor across a river. In the Harbardsljod, the two trade insults, with Harbard mocking Thor's poor clothes and suggesting that Sif has a lover, and Thor ends up walking around the water.

**Hrungnir**
A giant who drunkenly challenged Thor while feasting in Valhalla, after losing a horse race to Odin. In their duel Thor's hammer shattered Hrungnir's whetstone, a piece of which lodged in Thor's head. The seeress Groa tried to sing it out, but stopped when Thor distracted her with news of her husband Aurvandil, whose frostbitten toe Thor had broken off and thrown into the sky as a star.

**Geirrod and the giantess Grid**
On his way to the giant Geirrod, Thor received a magic belt, iron gloves, and a staff from the giantess Grid. He killed Geirrod by catching a red-hot iron bolt the giant threw and hurling it back through a pillar.

**Megingjord and Jarngreipr**
Thor's belt of strength, which doubles his power, and his iron gloves, which he needs to wield Mjolnir. Together with the hammer they make up his main possessions.

**Kicking Litr into Baldr's pyre**
During Baldr's funeral, Thor blessed the pyre with his hammer and, annoyed when the dwarf Litr ran in front of him, kicked Litr into the flames.

**Family and home**
Thor is the son of Odin and the earth giantess Jord, the husband of Sif, and the lover of the giantess Jarnsaxa. His sons Magni and Modi inherit Mjolnir after Ragnarok, and his daughter is Thrud. He lives in Thrudvangar (Thrudheim), in the hall Bilskirnir with 540 rooms.

**Svadilfari's master**
Thor killed the giant mason who was building the walls of Asgard, after the giant became enraged when Loki, disguised as a mare, lured away his stallion Svadilfari.
